text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- President Lennart Meri said he was disappointed over Bonn's position on NATO enlargement and regretted that Germany had not fulfilled its promise to act as an advocate for a speedy admittance of the Baltic countries into NATO and the EU.
- Finnish Defence Minister Anneli Taina and Estonian Defence Minister Andrus Oovel dismiss the claims of Estonian daily Eesti Paevaleht that Oovel insulted his Finnish counterpart.
- There are positive signs in Estonian-Russian relations and there is no disagreement within the Estonian government over its eastern policy, Foreign Minister Siim Kallas said.
- Estonian writer Jaan Kross has been presented as a candidate for the 1996 Nobel literature award.
- Music lovers in Tallin were presented two pianos in the Estonian Concert Hall -- a Steinway grand and a new version of the piano Estonia.

- Five million kroons have been allocated by the government to provide loans for young teachers; 30 teachers from rural areas have signed agreements for two million kroons, teachers in cities can apply for a loan from October 1.
- Chairman of the Pro Patria (Fatherland Union) Toivo Jurgenson is the candidate of the Rightwing-Moderates electoral union for Mayor of Tallinn.
- The fire at the Oru peat field in northeastern Estonia is nearly out, rescue officials said yesterday.
- Russian Defence Minister Igor Rodionov expressed satisfaction that the Baltic states would not be admitted to NATO in the first stage of its enlargement.
- Several senior ministry officials are members of company boards, receiving a monthly pay that they have no nright to accept under the public service law.
